ego.name: Steve Jobs
ego.summary: Steve Jobs was an American businessman, inventor, and investor who co-founded Apple, founded NeXT, and served as chairman and majority shareholder of Pixar. He helped shape the personal-computer revolution and, after returning to Apple in 1997, led the development and marketing of products including the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad.

connections.relationship_description: Paul Jobs adopted Jobs as an infant and raised him in California. A machinist, he encouraged Jobs’s interest in mechanical craftsmanship through work in the family garage.
connections.notes: Jobs regarded Paul as his father and rejected language that diminished their relationship.

connections.relationship_description: Clara Jobs and Paul Jobs adopted Steve Jobs shortly after his birth. She helped raise him in California and supported his education.
connections.notes: Jobs regarded Clara and Paul as his parents.

connections.relationship_description: Patricia Jobs was adopted by Paul and Clara Jobs in 1957 and grew up with Steve Jobs in the Jobs family household.
connections.notes: She was known as Patty and also helped assemble early Apple circuit boards.

connections.relationship_description: Mona Simpson was Jobs’s biological younger sister. They first met in 1986 after their biological mother arranged a meeting. They became friends and searched for their father together.
connections.notes: Simpson later helped Jobs repair his relationship with his daughter Lisa.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs met Laurene Powell after his 1989 Stanford Business School lecture. They married in 1991 and raised three children together.
connections.notes: Their marriage lasted until Jobs's death in 2011.

connections.relationship_description: Chrisann Brennan was Jobs’s first girlfriend at Homestead High School and an on-and-off partner for about five years. They were the parents of Lisa Brennan-Jobs.
connections.notes: Their relationship became strained after Jobs initially denied paternity of their daughter.

connections.relationship_description: Reed Jobs was the son of Steve Jobs and Laurene Powell Jobs, born in 1991.
Erin Jobs was the daughter of Steve Jobs and Laurene Powell Jobs, born in 1995.
Eve Jobs was the daughter of Steve Jobs and Laurene Powell Jobs, born in 1998.
Steve Wozniak and Jobs became friends through Bill Fernandez in 1971 and sold blue boxes together. They co-founded Apple in 1976 to develop and market Wozniak’s early computers.
connections.notes: Wozniak designed the early computers while Jobs drove their commercialization and marketing.

connections.relationship_description: Kottke met Jobs at Reed College in 1972, traveled with him through India in 1974, and became an early Apple employee who helped build and test computer hardware.
connections.notes: Kottke lived with Jobs and Chrisann Brennan near Apple's Cupertino office and worked on Apple II, Apple III, and Macintosh prototypes.

connections.relationship_description: After Jobs returned to Apple, he worked closely with Ive on the company's industrial design direction and on products including the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad.
connections.notes: Jobs described Ive as his spiritual partner at Apple; Ive delivered eulogies at Jobs's employee and family memorial services.

connections.relationship_description: As Pixar's chairman and majority shareholder, Jobs worked with Lasseter, Pixar's leading creative figure, during the studio's emergence as a major animation company and the production of Toy Story.
connections.notes: Lasseter led Pixar's creative work while Jobs provided corporate leadership and long-term financial backing.

connections.relationship_description: Markkula met Jobs and Wozniak while they sought financing for Apple II production, invested critical early capital, helped incorporate Apple in 1977, and supplied managerial guidance.
connections.notes: Markkula later backed John Sculley during the 1985 dispute that led Jobs to leave Apple, but supported Jobs's return in 1997.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs recruited John Sculley from Pepsi to lead Apple in 1983. They later clashed over management and product strategy, and Apple’s board supported Sculley in 1985.
connections.notes: Their early partnership helped launch the Macintosh, but their conflict resulted in Jobs's resignation and creation of NeXT.

connections.relationship_description: Jobs recruited Tim Cook to Apple in 1998, and they built a close executive partnership during Apple’s revival. Cook managed operations and succeeded Jobs as Apple CEO.
connections.notes: Cook led much of Apple's day-to-day business during Jobs's medical leaves while Jobs continued making major strategic decisions.

connections.relationship_description: Schieble arranged Jobs's closed adoption in 1955 and later helped arrange his introduction to his biological sister Mona Simpson in 1986.
connections.notes: Their relationship was separated by the circumstances of Jobs's adoption.

connections.relationship_description: Lisa Brennan-Jobs was Jobs's daughter with Chrisann Brennan. After initially denying paternity, Jobs later accepted it, reconciled with Lisa, and legally added his surname to hers.
connections.notes: Their later relationship remained complex and is central to Lisa Brennan-Jobs's memoir Small Fry.

connections.relationship_description: Ronald Wayne worked with Jobs and Steve Wozniak at Atari and helped mediate an early discussion about their venture. He drafted Apple’s original partnership agreement and became a co-founder in April 1976.
connections.notes: Wayne withdrew from Apple less than two weeks after its formation because of his financial exposure.

connections.relationship_description: Bushnell, Atari's co-founder, hired Jobs as a computer technician and assigned him the Breakout circuit-board project, for which Jobs enlisted Steve Wozniak's engineering help.
connections.notes: Bushnell characterized Jobs as difficult but valuable.

category_summaries.summary: Adoption shaped Jobs’s early family life in the Santa Clara Valley, where Paul and Clara Jobs raised him. His later connection with his biological mother and sister opened another branch of the family. He built a household with Laurene Powell Jobs and their children. His relationship with Chrisann Brennan and Lisa Brennan-Jobs remained difficult after his initial denial of Lisa’s paternity.

Jobs’s innovation circle joined engineering, industrial design, and animation. Steve Wozniak supplied the early computer designs that Jobs brought to market through Apple. After Jobs returned to Apple, Jony Ive made industrial design central to products such as the iMac, iPod, and iPhone. At Pixar, John Lasseter led the studio’s creative work while Jobs provided corporate leadership and long-term financial backing.

Business partners and executives shaped Jobs’s ability to build companies. Mike Markkula provided early Apple capital and management guidance. Conflict with John Sculley and Apple’s board forced Jobs out in 1985. After Jobs returned, Tim Cook became Apple’s operations leader and later succeeded him as chief executive.
